Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 105, English)
Sant Mahima: How a Mantra Builds Shielding, Siddhi, and Why Sadhaks Feel "Attacked" — and a Warning Against Fake Tantric Cur es

This session opens with a welcome to Ashaeiynn and an overview of what the institute offers, followed by a live havan (with a first-time devotee's r egistration), and then a detailed teaching on "sant mahima" (the glory/power of saints) — how mantra practice builds layer ed pr otection and siddhi in the body , why advanced sadhaks periodically feel sudden unexplained pain or pr essur e, and a pointed warning against fraudulent practitioners who diagnose fake "masaani kriya" curses to pr ofit fr om frightened devotees. The session continues as a New Y ear's Eve gathering, including the story of devotee Rohit Bhai's faith and the establishing of the Rameshwar Sarkar Shivling at Ashaeiynn, an extended individual checking r ound (with a firm warning against donation/goshala fraud), a congr egational prayer with an akhand-deepak sankalp, and a closing teaching on "samay" (time) as a guru's truest gift.
Part A — Welcome to Ashaeiynn

1. Opening framing: The speaker welcomes the group, describing Ashaeiynn as "a magical city" where remarkable things happen through the power of Ram naam, and frames the moment as the right time for each devotee to understand, observe, and learn this subject.

2. Ashaeiynn as an autonomous institute: The speaker describes Ashaeiynn as "an autonomous institute" that works continuously on this spiritual power , of fering every new devotee a personal mentor/guide for questions on any topic — spiritual guidance, payments, receipts, registration, enrollment, or personal concerns — plus a grievance department for complaints and access to the Ashaeiynn app.

3. What the Ashaeiynn app offers: Per this teaching, after 12:00 pm the app provides access to a continuous Ram havan session where a devotee can, from home, work to clear negativity , ancestral (pitru) issues, and tantric obstruction, awaken kundalini shakti and chakras, and work toward drishti and darshan of deities and the paralaukik (otherworldly) realm; it also provides access to Mool Tatva teaching videos.

4. A claim about consistent viewing: The speaker states that a devotee who watches all Mool Tatva videos while doing their jaap can expect to understand roughly 95% of the subtle world completely , with the remaining 5% described as continuously changing day to day — meaning, per this teaching, that no one can honestly claim to have "fully" understood the subtle world, since it is inherently dynamic.

5. A guarantee tied to sincer e practice: Per this teaching, a devotee who follows proper method (vidhi-vidhan), sustains jaap, participates in rituals and yagna, and studies the available teachings cannot ultimately be prevented from receiving darshan and drishti — and various bindings/obstructions are said to resolve even from home through this practice.

6. Ashaeiynn's r ole for negativity and tantric obstruction: Per this teaching, most devotees do not actually need to travel to Ashaeiynn in person for negativity or tantric-obstruction issues — relief is generally available from home; only in select critical
cases are devotees invited to Ashaeiynn in person, where such issues are typically resolved within three to four days.

7. Community identity and the single mantra/guru: As stated repeatedly in this lineage's teaching, Ashaeiynn uses a single mantra ("Jai Siyaram") and recognizes a single guru (Sri Hanuman ji Maharaj), operating within a lineage (parampara) of gurus and described as "a stronghold of saints" rather than the primary seat of any single deity .

8. Ashaeiynn's weekly schedule: Per this teaching, the institute's activities run seven days a week without a day of f: Monday negativity sessions, Tuesday–W ednesday shaktipat, Thursday kul devata readings, Saturday mantra chanting, and Sunday Mool Tatva teaching.

9. The purpose of Mool Tatva sessions: Per this teaching, Mool Tatva sessions convey the same subtle-world knowledge that some devotees acquire directly through drishti — and the underlying subtle world's principle is not "learn it once and stop," but continuous adaptation, since the subtle world itself changes daily .

10. A first-time havan r egistration: The session opens its practical portion with a first-time devotee completing havan registration through the guide/mentor system (name, family details, and address collected for registration purposes — omitted here for privacy) and being directed to the appropriate prayer/shielding section within the app for a first-time "shielding" havan.
Part B — How Mantra Builds Layer ed Shielding (Aura Shielding)

1. The cor e claim — sant mahima depends on mantra: In response to devotees' initial guesses (prayer power , guru parampara), the speaker states that sant mahima (a saint's glory/power) fundamentally depends on mantra.

2. Mantra as a multi-dimensional opener: Per this teaching, every mantra chanted — such as during a havan's ahuti (of fering) — opens "multi-dimension," meaning repeated mantra chanting progressively upgrades a devotee's own dimensional level from wherever they currently stand.

3. Twelve quantum points in the body: Per this teaching, after sustained chanting the mantra "correlates" fully with the practitioner's body , settling into twelve distinct points (described as "quantum points") distributed around the body .

4. The first three "kavach" (shields): Per this teaching, as three of these points become filled with mantra, a first protective shield (kavach) forms around the body on one plane (illustrated as the X-axis); as further points fill, second and third shields form on additional planes (Y -axis, Z-axis) — together covering the practitioner in three dimensional "planes" of shielding, compared by one devotee present to the childhood superhero Shaktimaan's protective aura.

5. Layer ed "plate" shielding thr ough r epeated aura-shielding sessions: Per this teaching, further sustained mantra practice adds additional shield layers stacked on top of the first three, resembling stacked plates; this is the stated purpose of the threeday "aura shielding" sessions of fered at Ashaeiynn.

6. Shields ar e initially empty — glow vs. dark: Per this teaching, these shield "plates," once granted by the lok's attendants (doot), start out empty; filling them with ongoing jaap makes them glow , while leaving them unfilled leaves them dark — with a properly glowing, jaap-filled shield making it ef fectively impossible for negativity to break through.

7. What can weaken this shielding: Per this teaching, roughly forty days entirely without prayer , jaap, or lamp-lighting can begin to weaken (though not instantly destroy) this shielding — described as breakable in principle, like any material, but even a small amount of prayer during that period is enough to preserve its protective ef fect.

8. On claims of "negativity getting in" despite consistent practice: Per this teaching, a devotee who maintains consistent jaap and practice yet insists negativity has entered their body regardless is, per the speaker , most likely dealing with unfounded fear (vaham) rather than an actual intrusion — and per this teaching, there is no remedy for vaham itself; it must be recognized and let go of directly .

9. Multi-layer shielding becomes visible with mor e practice: Per this teaching, with further jaap this layered shielding becomes visible as multiple distinct layers around a person — referencing a recent video in which one devotee's aura reading of another showed five distinct visible layers.
Part C — Mantra Devtas, Tarang, and Siddhi Types

1. Mantra devtas arrive to check a practitioner: Per this teaching, as mantra practice deepens further , the mantra's own devtas (deities) come to check the practitioner — assessing whether that person will, after death, be eligible to go to their particular lok (realm).

2. Sant appr oval is r equired first: Per this teaching, this evaluation requires surrender/compassion, and specifically requires a saint's approval — without which a devotee cannot access that lok, however sincere their practice; once a saint grants approval, a "tarang" (wave/vibration) is immediately received.

3. What a tarang is: Per this teaching, a tarang is described as a small vibration that carries a specific spiritual element, descending from above along with pranic ener gy and appearing, to those with drishti, as a moving line circulating through the practitioner's body .

4. The tarang activates kundalini and opens chakras: Per this teaching, sustained jaap eventually causes this tarang to strike the practitioner's kundalini shakti, opening it and revealing the ascending chakras one by one.

5. Which chakra a deity's pr esence settles on is determined by character , not fixed rule: Per this teaching, once chakras open, the tarang settles on whichever chakra corresponds to the practitioner's own emotional orientation toward a given deity — for example, settling on the heart chakra if a devotee loves that deity purely from the heart. Per this teaching, this is why two devotees of the same deity (e.g. Hanuman ji Maharaj) can show that deity's presence "seated" on entirely dif ferent chakras (one at the throat, one at the heart) — determined, per the speaker , by the devotee's own character rather than any fixed rule tied to the deity itself.

6. A settled tattva gr ows to eventually cover the whole body: Per this teaching, once a deity's tattva settles on a chakra, it continues to grow over time until it eventually envelops the practitioner's entire body , at which point the whole body itself functions as a single, lar ge chakra.

7. Two br oad types of siddhi — mantra siddhi and kripa siddhi: Per this teaching, siddhi generally comes in (at least) two forms: siddhi earned purely through one's own mantra practice ("mantra siddhi"), which brings "mantra doot" (mantraattendants); and siddhi received through a saint's direct grace ("kripa siddhi"), in which the granting saint sends one of their own subtle bodies to stand behind the devotee's aura, appearing as a "devdoot" (divine attendant/messenger).

8. Where each type of doot draws its ongoing energy fr om: Per this teaching, mantra doot are sustained by continued jaap itself, while devdoot are sustained by the same saint/source who originally granted them — meaning a devotee cannot "rechar ge" a devdoot through jaap alone; only the originating saint can continue fueling it.
Part D — Why Sadhaks Suddenly Feel Pain: The "Potential Differ ence" Teaching

1. The problem: mantra doot and devdoot can "clash": Per this teaching, a devotee who accumulates both mantra doot (which continue increasing with ongoing jaap) and a devdoot (which does not increase the same way) can experience a clash between the two — illustrated as the devotee's attention being pulled in two directions by competing guidance.

2. The "potential differ ence" analogy: Per this teaching, borrowing the electrical concept of potential dif ference (voltage dif ference between two points), when one source of spiritual ener gy is much "higher" than another connected to the same

practitioner , ener gy flows rapidly from the higher to the lower — and this flow itself is what produces a dramatic, sudden ef fect ("magic") such as multiple chakras activating all at once, more than a practitioner may feel able to handle.

3. Why this causes a brief shielding gap and sudden pain: Per this teaching, during the short transition window (illustrated as roughly two to three seconds, later refined to a twelve-to-thirteen-second range) it takes for this ener gy to equalize between the two points, the practitioner's protective shielding briefly drops toward zero — and it is specifically during this narrow window that sudden, otherwise-unexplained pain (commonly at the chest/heart-chakra area) can occur , described as a kind of "system reboot."

4. This is not evidence of an external tantric attack: Per this teaching, this sudden pain is not caused by any external entity , ancestor (pitru), or hostile tantric attack — it is a natural consequence of the practitioner's own accumulating siddhis and shifting "riders" (spiritual influences) transitioning within their own body , and should be understood as such rather than feared.

5. A pointed warning against fraudulent "masaani kriya" diagnoses: The speaker directly and firmly criticizes practitioners (referred to as "dhongi baba," fraudulent godmen) who diagnose sudden pain of this kind as evidence of a masaani kriya (a graveyard/tantric ritual curse, e.g. an inverted of fering to Kali) and char ge devotees for a "twelve gole" ritual to remove it — stating plainly that this is not how any real af fliction of that kind would actually be resolved, and that Ashaeiynn has never , in its own experience, encountered or needed to "extract" any devotee's masaani in this manner .

6. The speaker's stated basis for this claim: The speaker notes that over 500 documented videos of devotees whose drishti has opened are publicly available on the channel, of fered as evidence that these outcomes come from sustained practice, not theatrical claims about curses.

7. Encouraging self-r esponsibility over externalized blame: Per this teaching, sudden discomfort during deepening practice should be met with self-understanding rather than panic or external blame — the speaker uses the image of a child who runs, falls, and is picked up by their father , cautioning devotees against dramatizing ordinary growing pains as external attacks requiring divine rescue from a crisis they themselves triggered through their own progress.
Part E — Yagna as the Real Stabilizer

1. Yagna (havan) as the actual r emedy for this instability: Per this teaching, the genuine way to stabilize the fluctuating ener gy described above is yagna — of fering ghee, butter , and panchmeva (a mix of five dried fruits/nuts) into fire, a practice the speaker notes many devotees resist due to its cost or ef fort compared to jaap alone.

2. Historical practice and its er osion: Per this teaching, in earlier times devotees would of fer their own household's milk, ghee, butter , and panchmeva into yagna while living more simply themselves, on the principle that the body's own needs should be minimized in favor of what is of fered; the speaker laments that this discipline has eroded as modern emphasis has shifted toward personal bodily comfort over ritual of fering.

3. Why "riders" (spiritual influences) shifting also causes jolts: Per this teaching, as dif ferent saints/ener gies ("riders") cycle through association with an advancing practitioner's astral body , each transition can itself produce a jolt, since each rider has dif ferent characteristic preferences and intensities that the practitioner's body must adjust to.

4. Agni tattva (fir e element) as the balancing factor: Per this teaching, a practitioner whose fire element (agni tattva) is strongly developed at the astral level (not merely physically) is able to stabilize and balance many dif ferent saints' or ener gies' influence within their own body , since their chakras are already accustomed to unusually intense ener gy .

5. Closing guidance on the speaker's appr oach: The speaker states explicitly that this teaching is not intended to elevate, diminish, insult, or criticize anyone or anything, but purely to help devotees understand these mechanics more clearly , framing
Ashaeiynn as a research-oriented institute ("as a research scholar") continuously studying the astral world and sharing what is understood as understanding develops.

6. A closing practical question — personal havan practice: In response to a devotee who performs havan on his own, the speaker clarifies that doing so is fine only if the devotee has the appropriate permission; conducting havan, or changing its location, without proper permission/alignment can itself cause dif ficulty .
Part F — The Power of Faith: Rohit Bhai and the Establishing of Rameshwar Sarkar

1. The Rohit Bhai anecdote — faith without a formal target still "lands": The speaker recounts that a sadhna/blessing had originally been intended for another devotee ("Shivas Bhaiya"), but a devotee named Rohit Bhai, who prostrated (dandvat) in complete, uncalculating faith and expressed pure joy and gratitude, ended up receiving the benefit himself instead — of fered as a teaching that sincere, blind faith within this guru lineage can still yield real results even when a blessing was not formally addressed to that person.

2. The establishment of "Rameshwar Sarkar" (a Shivling) at Ashaeiynn: Per this teaching, a Shivling now called "Rameshwar Sarkar" was established at Ashaeiynn through a pandit referred to as "V ikas Bhaiya," whose own drishti (subtle sight) opened during the process of establishing it — of fered as the origin story behind this particular murti/shivling now used in the institute's rituals (including the rudra abhishek described in Part context below).

3. New Year's Eve framing: This session's gathering is framed partly as a New Year's Eve occasion, including a dinner break, a comic exchange with a devotee ("Dinesh bhai") about samosas, ice cream, and drishti, and light-hearted teasing among devotees about marriage matchmaking.
Part G — Extended Individual Checking Round: Negativity , Pitru, and a Warning Against Donation Fraud

1. Overview: Following the teaching in Parts A–F , the speaker conducted an extended live individual checking round in which devotees came forward one at a time to have their aura, negativity , and pitru (ancestral) status checked, receive guidance, and in many cases receive an ener getic cleansing ("jhaada"). Given the very lar ge number of devotees checked, this round is summarized here in aggregate rather than reproduced name-by-name, consistent with this project's established convention for roll calls and checking rounds.

2. General pattern observed: The lar ge majority of devotees checked showed no negativity and no pitru influence, often alongside visible "siddhi" (a settled mantra tattva) attributed to consistent japa; a smaller group showed mild pitru presence (commonly linked to minor aches, vibration sensations, or emotional heaviness) resolved through continued diya/prayer; and a small number showed active negativity or a lingering tantric element requiring an ener getic "cut" during the session itself, with the speaker frequently reassuring devotees that visible improvement ("halka lagna") during the checking itself is normal and expected.

3. Distinguishing ordinary pitru pr esence from active pitru "kriya": Per this teaching, when a devotee's protective shielding (built through consistent japa and kavach) becomes too strong for a stuck ancestor (pitru) to penetrate directly , that pitru may instead "give an of fering" (bhog) to a dif ferent, unrelated entity and ef fectively outsource an attack to it — so a devotee may feel classic "kriya" (ritual-attack) symptoms even though no living tantric practitioner is tar geting them, and the true root cause remains an unresolved pitru issue. The recommended response is not to fight the entity that appears, but to pray specifically that any such kriya be resolved by the responsible pitru itself being restrained ("kriya kate, kriya katte hi pitra pitaye").

4. A reminder on personal/home havan practice: As in Part E, devotees performing havan at home on their own are reminded this is acceptable only with proper permission/alignment; changing a havan's established location or method without this
permission can itself cause dif ficulty .

5. Never change your chosen mantra: In response to a devotee's question about a shifting ener gy pattern after visiting an external mantra/shakti source, the speaker reiterates a standing rule: a devotee should keep one mantra for life, regardless of which deity or shrine they visit, of fering their existing mantra in surrender at every altar rather than adopting a new one — switching mantras repeatedly is described as a frequent cause of instability , since a new "mantra doot" competing with an already-settled one is what produces disruptive symptoms (per the "potential dif ference" teaching in Part D).

6. On personal side-practices (e.g., Sri Vidya sadhna): A devotee who has practiced a separate, long-standing sadhna (in this case Sri Vidya, for several years) was told this need not be abandoned — such a practitioner can continue their existing sadhna alongside Ashaeiynn's mantra practice, splitting daily time between the two (e.g., roughly equal morning and evening sessions), with the existing sadhna dedicated in Ashaeiynn's guru-sankalp for stability . What currently reads as unsettled "negativity" around such a practitioner was described as likely to mature into a settled siddhi rather than something to fear .

7. Reassurance for devotees with spontaneous unsettling impr essions: A devotee who described occasionally and involuntarily perceiving disturbing figures (e.g., a menacing female apparition near a colleague) was reassured this reflects good drishti/siddhi rather than danger , and was cautioned against praying to make such perceptions stop unless they come with genuine physical harm — suppressing this kind of perception out of discomfort, per this teaching, tends to shut the ability down rather than resolve the underlying concern.

8. A firm public warning against donation and goshala (cow-shelter) fraud: The speaker states unambiguously and at length that Ashaeiynn does not operate, and has never operated, any goshala, and that no member or mentor is authorized to collect donations — for a goshala or for any other purpose — into a personal bank account. Devotees wishing to donate toward cowwelfare are told to pay a registered goshala directly via its own scanner and to obtain a receipt; anyone claiming Ashaeiynn or the speaker personally authorized a personal-account payment should be reported immediately to the grievance department. The only material contribution the institute asks for is bringing ghee, samagri, or similar items in person to the ongoing yagna; taking or accepting money "in Ashaeiynn's name" for any other purpose is described as explicitly outside institute policy , and misuse of donations collected in a cow's name is called out as a serious wrongdoing that would not be tolerated from any member , regardless of standing.

9. A devotee's financial-struggle question, and the astral-compensation principle: In response to a devotee describing years of financial dif ficulty , the speaker reiterates a broader principle also seen elsewhere in this teaching series — that if one area of a person's life is made deliberately dif ficult, another is typically strengthened in balance (here, astral/spiritual capacity) — and recommends building astral strength through the same standard roadmap: clearing negativity , receiving drishti, then progressing to aura shielding, chakra-opening havan, and siddhi, after which the devotee should return for guidance on next-stage sadhna suited to their existing skills (in this case, reiki, tarot, and astrology).

10. Practical case — sustained japa r ecommended for a mobility-impair ed devotee: A devotee unable to walk without support was told this reflects an astral-world (not purely medical) obstruction, and was advised to commit to roughly eight hours of japa daily (or in broken two-hour blocks) for forty days, alongside continued yagna attendance, with the promise of guidance on further steps once that period is completed.

1 1. Session boundary: The speaker explicitly closed this extended checking round ("aaj ke liye ye data yahi samapt rehta hai" — today's data collection ends here) before the group moved on to a separate, dedicated Mahashivratri Rudra Abhishek ritual (processed as a separate session in this project, given its own distinct opening sankalp, registration list, and closing sankalp).
Part H — Congr egational Prayer , Akhand Deepak Sankalp, and the Teaching on "Samay" (T ime) as the Guru's True Gift

1. Congr egational chanting and formal invocation: The gathering moved into extended congregational "Sitaram"/"Jai Siyaram" chanting, followed by a formal Sanskrit invocation ("Om asya shri Ram tarak mantrasya...") naming Sita as rishi and citing the Gayatri and Anushtup chhand, alongside a prayer bowing to Dharti Mata (Mother Earth).

2. The akhand-deepak (continuous lamp) sankalp: A long dedication list naming roughly 85 devotees was read aloud for a collective akhand-deepak sankalp (continuous-lamp dedication) — summarized here in aggregate rather than reproduced nameby-name, consistent with this project's established treatment of long roll calls — followed by a collectively recited sankalp prayer of fering the lamp, jaap, and tapasya in the guru's name and requesting Ram tattva, mantra, shakti, bhakti, and drishti.

3. The cor e teaching: "samay" (time) as the true gift a guru/saint gives: Building on the Rohit Bhai anecdote (Part F), the speaker teaches that what a genuine guru or saint ultimately of fers a devotee is not wealth or an instant fix, but time — the willingness to walk alongside a devotee's growth at whatever pace it takes.

4. The hospital-vs-r oadside-cur e parable: Per this teaching, a slower , more thorough remedy (likened to proper hospital treatment) is preferable to a fast but shallow "roadside" fix (likened to a folk remedy of dust or similar) — genuine healing/growth takes time, and this is not a flaw in the process.

5. The story of Karna's Nagastra and Hanuman saving Arjun: The speaker retells the Mahabharata episode in which Karna's Nagastra (serpent-weapon), aimed at Arjuna, was diverted by Krishna pressing the chariot down, and Hanuman ji Maharaj (seated atop Arjuna's chariot banner) is credited with helping shield Arjuna in that critical moment — of fered as an illustration of divine intervention that unfolds within a single decisive moment, made possible by prior devotion.

6. The story of the Pashupatastra and Sita Mata saving Hanuman: A parallel story is of fered in which Hanuman ji, facing the Pashupatastra (Shiva's ultimate weapon) during his search for Sita in Lanka, is protected because the weapon recognizes and defers to Sita Mata's presence/protection over him — again illustrating how devotion and relationship, not brute ef fort alone, secure divine protection at the decisive moment.

7. "Yatra yatra raghunath kirtanam" — Hanuman's only true r equest: The speaker explains this well-known verse (describing Hanuman ji appearing with folded hands and tearful eyes wherever Lord Raghunath's (Rama's) glory is sung) as showing that Hanuman ji's only real request of Rama, across his long life of service, was for "time" spent in Rama's presence/kirtan — reinforcing the session's core teaching that time, not material reward, is the highest boon a devotee can seek or a guru can give.

8. Closing: The session concludes with the New Year's celebration continuing informally after the formal gathering ends (dance, informal socializing), and a closing "Jai Siyaram" send-of f to all present.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Sant mahima (a saint's power/glory) is described in this teaching as fundamentally dependent on mantra; sustained mantra practice progressively "upgrades" a practitioner's dimensional level and builds layered protective shielding (aura shielding) around the body . Shielding "plates" granted by a lok's attendants start empty; sustained jaap fills and makes them glow (protective), while roughly forty days without any prayer , jaap, or lamp-lighting can begin to weaken them. Persistent claims of "negativity getting in" despite consistent practice are, per this teaching, most often unfounded fear (vaham), which has no separate remedy beyond recognizing and releasing it. Deepening practice brings mantra devta evaluation (requiring a saint's approval) and a "tarang" that activates kundalini and opens chakras; which chakra a deity's presence settles on depends on the devotee's own emotional character , not a fixed rule. Two types of siddhi are described: mantra siddhi (bringing mantra doot, sustained by ongoing jaap) and kripa siddhi (bringing a devdoot, sustained only by the originating saint).

Sudden, unexplained pain (often at the chest/heart-chakra) during advancing sadhna is explained in this teaching as a natural "potential dif ference" ener gy-transition ef fect between dif ferent siddhis/riders within one's own body — not an external tantric or ancestral attack. The speaker firmly warns against fraudulent practitioners who diagnose sudden pain as a "masaani kriya" curse and char ge for a "twelve gole" removal ritual — stating this is not a legitimate remedy and that Ashaeiynn has never needed or used such a practice. Yagna (havan), of fering ghee/butter/panchmeva into fire, is presented as the genuine remedy for ener gy instability — historically paired with personal simplicity , a discipline the speaker says has eroded over time. A well-developed fire element (agni tattva) at the astral level allows a practitioner to stabilize many dif ferent saints'/ener gies' influence within their body as spiritual "riders" change. Sincere, uncalculating faith (illustrated by the Rohit Bhai anecdote) can yield real results within this guru lineage even without a formally addressed blessing; the Rameshwar Sarkar Shivling was established at Ashaeiynn through a pandit whose own drishti opened in the process. Devotees should never change their chosen mantra, even when visiting other shrines or deities — surrendering the existing mantra everywhere is taught as far more stable than adopting new ones, which can trigger disruptive "potential dif ference" symptoms. Ashaeiynn firmly states it operates no goshala and never authorizes personal-account donations in its name for any purpose — all such solicitations should be treated as fraud and reported. The guru's true gift to a devotee, per this teaching's closing discourse, is time (samay) rather than wealth or an instant fix — illustrated through the Karna/Nagastra/Hanuman, Pashupatastra/Sita Mata, and "yatra yatra raghunath kirtanam" stories. This teaching is of fered in a spirit of research and understanding, not to elevate or diminish anyone or anything.
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 105, English)
Sant Mahima: How a Mantra Builds Shielding, Siddhi, and Why Sadhaks Feel "Attacked" — and a Warning Against Fake Tantric Cur es

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this session's welcome overview , Sant Mahima teaching, the Rohit Bhai/Rameshwar Sarkar story , the extended checking r ound, and the closing teaching on "samay" (time).

Q1. What is Ashaeiynn, per this teaching's opening framing? A: Per this teaching, Ashaeiynn is described as "an autonomous institute" working continuously on this spiritual power , of fering every devotee a personal mentor/guide, a grievance department, and access to the Ashaeiynn app.

Q2. What does the Ashaeiynn app offer , per this session? A: Per this teaching, after 12:00 pm the app provides a continuous Ram havan session for clearing negativity , ancestral (pitru) issues, and tantric obstruction, awakening kundalini and chakras, and working toward drishti and darshan — plus access to Mool Tatva teaching videos.

Q3. What is Ashaeiynn's weekly schedule? A: Per this teaching, activities run seven days a week: Monday negativity sessions, Tuesday–W ednesday shaktipat, Thursday kul devata readings, Saturday mantra chanting, and Sunday Mool Tatva teaching.

Q4. What does sant mahima (a saint's glory/power) fundamentally depend on, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, sant mahima fundamentally depends on mantra — not merely prayer power or guru lineage on its own.

Q5. What ar e the "twelve quantum points" and the first thr ee kavach (shields)? A: Per this teaching, sustained mantra chanting settles into twelve points around the body; as three fill, a first protective shield forms (illustrated as the X-axis), with further points producing second and third shields (Y -axis, Z-axis) — together three dimensional planes of shielding.

Q6. What determines whether a shield "glows" or stays dark? A: Per this teaching, shield "plates" start empty; ongoing jaap fills and makes them glow (protective), while leaving them unfilled leaves them dark, and roughly forty days entirely without prayer , jaap, or lamp-lighting can begin to weaken this shielding.

Q7. A devotee insists negativity is entering their body despite consistent practice — what does this teaching say? A: Per this teaching, this is most likely unfounded fear (vaham) rather than an actual intrusion, and there is no separate remedy for vaham beyond recognizing and releasing it directly .

Q8. What is a "tarang," and what triggers a mantra devta's evaluation of a practitioner? A: Per this teaching, a tarang is a small vibration carrying a spiritual element, received once a saint approves a devotee's readiness; mantra devtas then check whether the practitioner will be eligible for their lok after death, and a saint's approval is required before this evaluation can proceed.

Q9. What determines which chakra a deity's pr esence "settles" on?
